LESSON: PREPARATION OF ANIMAL PRODUCTS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: Food Production Processes
Topic 2.4: Preparation of Animal Products

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Preparation of Animal Products. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we process fresh fish?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain the importance of processing fish and dressing poultry carcass

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PREPARATION OF ANIMAL PRODUCTS
Subject: AGRICULTURE · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Preparation of Animal Products helps you succeed in AGRICULTURE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS ABOUT ANIMALS
Animals are living things. They move, feed, grow, and respond to their surroundings.
Domestic animals live with people (cow, goat, chicken, dog, cat).
Wild animals live on their own in forests, parks, or water (lion, zebra, fish).
In Kenya you may see cows in a homestead, fish at a market, or birds on the school field.
Safety: do not touch unknown animals; wash hands after handling pets or farm animals.

PART 1: Explain the importance of processing fish and dressing poultry carcass

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the importance of processing fish and dressing poultry carcass. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the importance of processing fish and dressing poultry carcass.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Preparation of Animal Products” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the importance of processing fish and dressing poultry carcass. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Preparation of Animal Products is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Domestic animals live with people (cow, goat, chicken, dog, cat).

Wild animals live on their own in forests, parks, or water (lion, zebra, fish).

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Preparation of Animal Products” around your school. (skill: explain the importance of processing fish and dressing poultry carcass)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Preparation of Animal Products to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain the importance of processing fish and dressing poultry carcass.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Preparation of Animal Products from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Preparation of Animal Products: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Preparation of Animal Products?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we process fresh fish?
2. How can we dress poultry carcass?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Preparation of Animal Products means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain the importance of processing fish and dressing poultry carcass.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
